comment: Declarations read by tools/lock_discipline_check.py (rules R1-R10). A declaration closes an ANALYSIS gap; it never proves the declared contract. Every exception carries its why. Lock names: O owner/store, G gate, R roster, C commit, W consumer wait, L payload lifecycle, A arena pins, E extent realizer, K log kernel, S log spare, Q log queue, J service-log fallback, M mux inbox, X* leaf module locks. The realization rows are SEEDED here until the host-model book's *fn-hmc-realization* defconst lands; then they are generated from it (one authoritative copy).

S.why_io: serializes spare preparers; creation, preallocation and the fence run under it by design, never under O (io.lisp:6333-6337)

XDURABLE.why_io: serializes the two callers of fnn-log-make-durable (the new segment's first fence and the publication) so a rotated segment's name is fenced once and a failed barrier is recorded once and never retried (io.lisp:8498-8541); the file and directory fsyncs under it are its whole purpose. It is taken in no other place, so it guards nothing but that fsync pair and one nested kernel update (K); a caller that holds O does so on its own and is reported under O

J.why_io: the fallback service-log writer: written only while no writer thread runs (offline commands), io.lisp:1117-1149

XSYNCER.why: Private typed syncer ledger/grants. Startup takes O then this leaf; runtime receipt drops it before completion callback, classification or owner entry.

XOUTPUT.why: Private typed output projection. Startup O precedes this leaf; semantic methods operate only private ledger, no live STATE/arena and no callback to O while held.

XWEB.why: lane lock-rows-2: the web face's completion/job mutex (host/native/web-host.lisp). Every acquisition is a short in-memory critical section over the face and connection records (job mailbox, completion cells, disposal claims, cleanup debts), or the wake descriptor protocol: fnn-web-wake-locked writes one byte to a non-blocking pipe and fnn-web-close-wakes-locked closes the two pipe ends under it so no publisher can write a closed fd. No other declared lock is taken inside it except the diagnostic writer queue (the cleanup-failure fnn-err of fnn-unwind-cleanups); the semantic actor's job wait releases it (condition-wait)
XWEB.why_io: only the wake pipe's one-byte write and its two closes; both ends are set non-blocking (fnn-web-start), so neither can wait

XCSP.why: lane lock-rows-2: the catchup spool worker's request/completion cell (host/native/catchup-spool.lisp). Pure in-memory phase transitions and the worker's own condition-wait; the descriptor I/O (fnn-csp-worker-perform) runs between two acquisitions, never inside one

XPFB.why: lane lock-rows-2: the peer-flight bank's ledger mutex (host/native/catchup-spool.lisp fnn-peer-flight-bank-drained/-draw/-work/-settle). Serializes the bank-private resource ledger (fn-rl-draw / fn-rl-settle on the bank's own ledger object, the pure fn-csp-/fn-pfr- helpers); no live Store, owner state, I/O or other lock inside

XFJ.why: lane lock-rows-2: one FNFD feed journal's append lock (host/native/owner.lisp, struct comment 'one append (write, fsync, phase) at a time'). Held by fnn-owner-feed-append and the feed batch writer/barrier, both off the owner mutex and under it (a feed tick or a bound submission's inline commit); no other declared lock is taken inside it
XFJ.why_io: the frame write and the append-barrier fsync are the lock's purpose: they must be serialized per journal and the barrier must follow the writes it covers under the same lock; a journal is private to its feed, so no other service path waits on it

XTRACE.why: lane lock-rows-2: the opt-in native trace collector's private mutex (host/native/trace.lisp fnn-trace-begin/-finish/-snapshot): a leaf taken by fnn-trace-span, and so by every fnn-owner-measured use, under whatever lock the measured form runs under; its critical sections only reserve or complete one row (no hook, I/O, ACL2 or other lock)

XOBS.why: lane ACTORS: the native observer's private record mutex (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-native-observation-reserve/-complete/-events): a leaf taken for a row update by fnn-with-observed-owner/-mutex and fnn-observed-condition-wait under whatever lock they observe; it calls no hook, I/O, ACL2 or other lock

XPWAKE.why: lane lock-model-gaps: one pull runtime's wake counter and waitqueue (host/native/pull-service.lisp:59-62, fnn-pull-runtime-wake :1085-1090, fnn-pull-wakes-seen :1092-1094, the timed wait fnn-pull-ready-wait :1096-1109). A leaf: every region is an increment, a read or a condition-broadcast/-wait on its own queue, with no call into the owner, a lock, the log or I/O while held.

XTLSKX.why: lane lock-model-gaps: the decided key exchange record *fnn-tls-kx* (host/native/tls-reload.lisp:68). A leaf with three regions (:72 a copy-list, :91 the decision's setq of the group list and record, :131 one tally bump through a pure ACL2 core call); ACL2's session-line core call and the log write at :130 run before it is taken, never under it.

XIDLEGC.why: CONVERGE-2 row 34: the idle collection's three per-process marks (host/native/owner.lisp *fnn-idle-gc-tick-mark*, -collect-mark, -quiet), ticked by the maintenance worker or by a one-connection run's accept loop. A leaf: two in-memory regions in fnn-owner-maybe-collect-idle, the count and verdict (two pure ACL2 core calls, fn-idle-gc-quiet and fn-idle-gc-decide) and the marks after the collection; the collection runs between them, never under the lock.

lock_order.comment: the declared partial order (deputy section 1c + Astra 3.3 + Astra D7's added edges O->M, E->Q, A->Q); transitively closed by the check Lane ACTORS: XOBS (the observer's record mutex) nests under every observed lock; E -> XCRYPTO (host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-limit-serialized publishes the limit record under the extent mutex: the stage name's random hex takes *fnn-random-state-lock*, a leaf). Lane lock-rows-2: O -> XFJ (a feed tick or a bound submission appends under the owner mutex) and O -> XTRACE (fnn-trace-span, so fnn-owner-measured, takes the opt-in trace collector leaf); O -> SL and S -> SL (SL, fnn-log-spare-slot-lock, guards only the log's spare slot and its close debt, held for no I/O: the rotation under O and the preparers under S meet there); O -> XCLOSEDEBT and E -> XCLOSEDEBT (XCLOSEDEBT, *fnn-close-debts-lock*, guards the two close-debt lists *fnn-immutable-close-debts* and *fnn-publication-close-debts*, a leaf held for no I/O: any writer that stages a file pushes or observes there, so the edge is declared from the two holders the check reaches); R -> XMUXSLOT (fnn-mux-adopt reads and increments the round-robin cursor under the slot lock inside the roster section, for the once client) and XMUXSLOT -> M (fnn-mux-slot-observation reads each loop under the loop lock, called under the service's slot lock, a defstruct-slot mutex the check verifies: locks XMUXSLOT struct_slot); XWEB, S, XSYNCER -> Q (fnn-unwind-cleanups logs a failed cleanup with fnn-err, which offers its line to the writer queue, under the lock the cleanup runs in; Q is the terminal log queue).

fnn-section-envelope.why: the one envelope (def-section): its own template runs the body inside fnn-owner-shared-action-locked (tests.test_native_owner NativeOwnerHandlerStructureTests)

dominated_escape_functions.fnn-escape-cleanup-failed: io.lisp:553-582: called by fnn-unwind-cleanups only when the body is escaping (the not-completed arm, io.lisp:603-604) and a cleanup failed. It records each failure in *fnn-escape-cleanup-debts*, escalates ACL2's fn-fs-stop-exit-escalate over the primary's code and every failure's code (each floored at a fault), and returns normally ONLY when that code equals the primary's own (io.lisp:575-577: the escape in flight already outranks every cleanup failure, and goes on as itself); otherwise it signals fnn-indeterminate or fnn-fault (io.lisp:580-582). A cleanup failure is therefore never converted into success.

classifying_escape_functions.fnn-owner-thread-escape: owner.lisp:3025-3046: classifies the condition with ACL2's fn-fs-classify (fn-fs-classify-job with JOBP), books/failure-scope.lisp:92-112: an indeterminate class gives :indeterminate and calls fnn-owner-fence-service (3042); every fault class and any unknown serious condition gives :fault and calls fnn-owner-fault-service (3045); only refusal, usage and (JOBP, early OS error) job-failure kinds are answered to the caller unfenced (3044). A fault- or indeterminate-class condition handed to it therefore always reaches the fence or the fault stop.

owner-live-state.why: the served stobjs and *the-live-state* belong to the owner section (io.lisp:215-221, :319-336)

extent-pool.why: the cold pool and the realizer buffer: the extent mutex serializes them (extent.lisp:197)

control-buffer.why: the control buffer, filled and decoded under its lock (control-transport.lisp:19)

serving_roots.fnn-owner-accept: the primary accept/SIGTERM loop runs on the caller thread of fnn-owner-run after startup (owner.lisp:5959ff)

fnn-pull-worker-guarded.why: lane lock-model-gaps: the guarded wrapper of the pull worker (host/native/pull-service.lisp:1196-1200). The running host never calls it: fnn-pull-service-start spawns (lambda () (fnn-pull-worker runtime)) under the def-actor starter's own escape (:1205-1222), and only tests/native_feed_credential_raw-mock.lisp:201 calls the wrapper. Without this row it counts as a second, main-thread actor of everything the pull worker touches.

fnn-err.why: lane lock-model-gaps-2: the host's stderr diagnostic (host/native/io.lisp:1004). A handler whose protected form calls only a diagnostic sink and whose clause does nothing (ignore-errors, or a clause body that is empty or a constant) swallows the sink's own failure, which by construction carries no custody or classification: R7 does not ask it to reach the fence (fnn-log-physical-close :1101 after the debt is pushed under the queue mutex). The checker verifies that the sink's call closure reaches no fence function and no descriptor open or close primitive, and that each exempted handler's protected form calls nothing else.

fnn-bpnode-app-result.why: lane lock-model-gaps-2: host/native/bp-node.lisp:218-228 answers an indeterminate Store/FNRJ/FNWF result as (values :uncertain ...) and its only caller, fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one (:319-341), converts that status back to fnn-indeterminate (:339-341) after driving the delivery effects. The checker verifies the clause ends in (values :uncertain ...) without an early exit, that every reference to the function is a multiple-value-bind value form, and that the bound status reaches (when (eq STATUS :uncertain) (fnn-indeterminate ...)) past no return-from/return/go/throw. The R7 rule then reads the clause as a deferred rethrow, not a swallow.

dead_call_arms.why: lane lock-model-gaps-2: the mux loop never waits for a cold page (owner.lisp:6310-6326). fnn-owner-handle-chunk-step answers (values :cold READ) when the read's first value is :fnn-extent-cold and calls fnn-owner-chunk-results only in the else branch (:6339-6343); chunk-results calls fnn-owner-cold-line, which awaits the page, only in its :fnn-extent-cold arm (:5698). Reached through that one edge the arm is dead, so R9 does not count the await. The checker verifies the guard, that the argument is an unassigned local, and that every call to cold-line in chunk-results sits in that arm; the other callers of chunk-results (fnn-owner-handle-chunk, fnn-owner-cold-line itself) are not pruned.

fnn-pull-worker.why: lane lock-debt-rethrow (LOCK-R7-PULL-WORKER-DEBT-RETHROW): the release handler of fnn-pull-worker (pull-service.lisp:1181-1194) captures the first cleanup condition in FAILURE and, with a primary escape in flight, stores it in the runtime's cleanup-debt (:1192) rather than signalling, which would supersede the primary. fnn-pull-service-close signals it (:1259-1260), a retained debt blocks removal of the runtime (:1229), and the close runs as a close hook of the owner's stop path (operator-live.lisp:120-123, owner.lisp:1625, :8865-8868). The checker verifies each link: the capture, the store past no early exit, that the store is the only write of the slot, that the closer signals the slot on its spine before any early exit, that every other removal from the registry checks the slot, and that a binding of the close-hooks special names the closer, a constructor stores it as :close-hooks and a stop function funcalls each hook and tests its failure flag, both reached from inside that binding. Not verified: that the stop function's reaction to a failed hook (modules-joined nil, no clean exit) is itself the fence; that is owner.lisp's own logic.

dead_thread_guards.why: lane lock-model-gaps: the failed-start cleanup of fnn-mux-start (host/native/mux.lisp:1766-1801, the guard at :1791-1792) stops a loop on the starter's own thread only under (unless (and thread (sb-thread:thread-alive-p thread)) ...), where THREAD is looked up from that loop (fnn-mux-loop-thread, or the actor registered for it by fnn-owner-actor-for-custody): a loop whose thread is absent or no longer running. Everything the loop's thread did precedes that stop, so the stop is not concurrent with it. The check verifies the guard shape, that THREAD is bound from the object the call's first argument names, and that fnn-mux-start starts exactly one thread named "fn owner io"; that this thread is the one THREAD names is the code's, cited above.

fnn-observed-condition-wait.why: host/native/io.lisp:172: unchanged sb-thread:condition-wait on its (queue mutex) parameters plus observer rows; the checker verifies each condition-wait in the body waits on parameter MUTEX, so a call releases the lock its caller passes exactly as the primitive does

effect_overrides.fnn-err: bounded: a diagnostic is offered to the writer queue while the writer runs (io.lisp:843-849); the direct stderr write is the offline mode with no writer thread
effect_overrides.fnn-log-offer: bounded: queues under Q, never writes
effect_overrides.fnn-journal-line: bounded: offered to the writer, never written on the caller's thread (io.lisp:1122ff)
effect_overrides.fnn-developer-selector: developer-image environment read; production returns nil
effect_overrides.fnn-log-line: bounded: offered to the writer queue while the writer runs (io.lisp:1135-1149); the direct write under J is the offline/no-writer mode
effect_overrides.fnn-extent-executor-observe-returned: joins a cold worker only after observing it dead (extent.lisp:612-616): join-after-proven-termination, not a wait on a live worker

fnn-extent-prefetch.why: the token is issued under O+E before the worker runs (fn-pio-direct-admit) and released only after the job returns (books/page-read-direct.lisp, PRF-1234)

fnn-extent-window-run.why: a window job runs on the same persistent worker activation as an issued read

fnn-extent-decoded-window-pread.why: lane lock-rows-2: the decoded window's one physical read, called only by fnn-extent-decoded-window-run, which fnn-extent-executor-job runs on the persistent worker activation (extent.lisp, the decodedp arm) for a token fnn-extent-issue-window admitted through the decoded acquire; the descriptor is fetched under E in fnn-extent-decoded-window-run and the worker's actual return is announced by the loop only after the job returns

fnn-csp-worker-perform.why: the :digest/:replay pread is on the catchup spool's own temporary file, not an extent-registry descriptor: the worker thread opens it (catchup-spool.lisp:20, O_CREAT|O_EXCL, fnn-open) and unlinks the name at once, nothing else reads the slot, and the same thread closes it in the loop's cleanup (catchup-spool.lisp:77-81, the slot retired before the close). The check verifies those facts over the source, so a second toucher of the slot, a store from anywhere but that open, or a second thread running the loop breaks the row

fnn-snapshot-source-read-page.why: snapshot page lease: acquired under O+E, released in the unwind-protect cleanup or handed off (owner.lisp:4898-4917)

fn-pgs-fill-frame.why: The adopted image is a one-time registered process-lifetime root. The checker verifies immutable publication, reader identity/capture under E, close rejection before any registry close, and absence of other registry removers. No lock exemption.

lambda@host/native/bp-node.lisp:fnn-bpno.why: fnn-tcl-begin's :session-admit callback (channel admission, bp-node.lisp:998); bp-node serve's single serialized loop (fnn-bp-session-loop, specs/bp-node-machine.md 9.1): the callback is stored in the session grant or bound for its turn and called only from that loop's turns, on the command's thread, inside its dynamic extent, holding no lock. Re-declared 2026-10-05 (baseline-reds): lambda inserts had renumbered this ordinal, so the row's old text named the word callback (now #lambda1, undeclared: nothing it reaches needs a lock)

the *fnn-tcl-source-turn* binding of the grant's turn (bp-node.lisp:1019), funcalled by the tcl source machinery during fnn-tcl-turn; bp-node serve's single serialized loop (fnn-bp-session-loop, specs/bp-node-machine.md 9.1): the callback is stored in the session grant or bound for its turn and called only from that loop's turns, on the command's thread, inside its dynamic extent, holding no lock. Re-declared 2026-10-05 (baseline-reds): the row's old text named :session-admit (now #lambda2)

the *fnn-tcl-deliver* binding of the grant's turn (bp-node.lisp:1022), funcalled by fnn-tcl-session for one accepted connection during a turn; bp-node serve's single serialized loop (fnn-bp-session-loop, specs/bp-node-machine.md 9.1): the callback is stored in the session grant or bound for its turn and called only from that loop's turns, on the command's thread, inside its dynamic extent, holding no lock. Re-declared 2026-10-05 (baseline-reds): the row's old text named the grant's turn itself (now #lambda5, undeclared: nothing it reaches needs a lock)

lambda@host/native/bp-node.lisp:fnn-comm.why: *fnn-bpnode-control-pump*, let-bound by fnn-command-bp-node and funcalled by the node's own waits (bp-node.lisp:1127, audit-verified 2026-10-06); bp-node serve's single serialized loop (fnn-bp-session-loop, specs/bp-node-machine.md 9.1): the callback is stored in the session grant or bound for its turn and called only from that loop's turns, on the command's thread, inside its dynamic extent, holding no lock

lambda@host/native/bp-app.lisp:fnn-comma.why: bp-app receive's *fnn-tcl-deliver* binding (bp-app.lisp:379, audit-verified 2026-10-06), called by fnn-tcl-session for one accepted connection; fnn-accept-loop runs each handler to completion on the command's thread (io.lisp), no lock held

fnn-csp-worker-start.why: the catchup spool worker (catchup-spool.lisp:105-108): the thread is stored in the worker record before it is returned (the caller's retain, :105, publishes custody earlier); fnn-csp-worker-join-now (:143-151) joins it only once thread-alive-p is false; the loop turns a serious-condition from one operation into the status and condition the owner takes (:62, fnn-csp-worker-take :128-134), and a cleanup failure into cleanup-condition (:86) that join-now returns

fnn-dev-repl-start.why: the trusted developer REPL accept loop (dev-repl.lisp:216-235): the thread is stored in the control record, which *fnn-dev-repl* holds (:224), and fnn-dev-repl-close joins it (:247-256). It starts only when fnn-developer-selector finds FN_NATIVE_DEV_REPL, which is honoured only on a developer image (io.lisp:6958-6962), over a socket chmod 600 (dev-repl.lisp:205) whose peer must be the owner (:179); the loop prints a connection failure and keeps serving (:191), so a fault in an evaluation is the owner boundary's (fnn-dev-evaluate), never this thread's

allowed.*fnn-entry-guard-specs*: read-mostly guard-spec cache, filled once per entry name (io.lisp:1278); F6: to move to image build time

fnn-call.why: every condition in a core call becomes fnn-fault after the handler (io.lisp:1372-1393): converted, never swallowed

fnn-csp-worker-loop.why: the spool worker's condition is its RESULT: the loop stores it (catchup-spool.lisp:62, 68) and fnn-csp-worker-take re-signals any condition that is not an fnn-os-error as fnn-fault on the taking thread (catchup-spool.lisp:128-142), while an fnn-os-error stays the per-peer status :error ACL2 decides on

fnn-rc-window.why: ruling 19 (host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure): a condition a window of a live reconfiguration meets is the window's RESULT: fnn-rc-classify keeps it with the word ACL2's fn-orp-step takes (:uncertain, :refused or :fault), and the :fence or :fault effect the step answers re-signals it under the owner (fnn-rc-resignal, in a quantum of the caller's section), where the section's one boundary classifies it by its class and the publication step the window left

fnn-extent-executor-job.why: a cold job's fault is its RESULT, settled by the owner after actual return (extent.lisp:479-505)

fnn-log-sync-sealed-batch.why: the syncer returns :failed with its condition; the COMPLETE re-signals it under the owner (io.lisp:8043-8048)

fnn-owner-shared-action-locked.why: the fence boundary itself: its ignore-errors guard the connection's fault reply inside a clause that then stops the service

fnn-mux-loop-inbox.why: adopt registers under R and pushes under M; stop drains once and closes the wake fds (B2, r71 F9, S021)

fnn-mux-loop-arrived.why: await completions delivered after the loop's last drain (S021)

accept.why: the primary accept/SIGTERM loop must not wait at the gate (r71 F8)

mux-loop.why: an I/O loop must not park in a cold await (r71 F7)
mux-loop.why_await_ok: every served quantum waits for its admission at the gate (owner.lisp:1362); the check cannot separate an ordinary admission wait from r71 F7's :control settlement behind a barrier, which stays a MODEL obligation

close_sites.fnn-extent-close: the :close realization: closes a registered extent fd after fn-pio-file-clear-p (realization row :close)
close_sites.fnn-csp-worker-loop: the catch-up spool worker's own descriptor: fnn-csp-worker-perform's :open (O_EXCL, then unlink) on this worker thread stores it in the worker; the loop's exit retires the number, then closes it once (host/native/catchup-spool.lisp)
close_sites.fnn-log-physical-close: the log subsystem's consumed fd slots: the caller has already taken the descriptor out of its owner (io.lisp:1096 docstring 'Caller consumed its fd slot'); this closes it once and records the exact physical debt, never retried
close_sites.fnn-init-admit: the init stage lock descriptor fnn-init-stage-lock opened and flocked (io.lisp:4509, flock 4511); every admission exit unlocks and closes it here (io.lisp:4586)
close_sites.fnn-immutable-close-handle: the immutable publication's owning fd slot, consumed by the caller (io.lisp:5399); closed once here, an ambiguous return retained in *fnn-immutable-close-debts*, never retried
close_sites.fnn-log-close-active: the log's active segment descriptor held in the fnn-log struct (fnn-log-fd), opened by the log's open/rotate path; consumed and closed exactly once here, a failure retained as fnn-log-active-close-debt (io.lisp:8355)
close_sites.fnn-log-discard-spare: the staged spare's descriptor (the third of fnn-log-spare), opened by fnn-log-prepare-spare; closed and unlinked once here when the spare is not renamed, a failure retained as fnn-log-spare-close-debt (io.lisp:8371)
close_sites.fnn-tcl-spool-release: the transfer's spool lock descriptor handed to the release (tcpcl.lisp:278); unlocked and closed independently, an ambiguous return retained in *fnn-tcl-spool-close-debts*, never retried
close_sites.fnn-app-journal-close: the application journal's lock fd (fnn-app-journal-lock-fd), consumed here before the close (workflow.lisp:34); unlocked and closed once, custody of an ambiguous return retained via fnn-app-retain-close-debt

fnn-owner-install-or-end.why: host/native/owner.lisp: runs the off-mutex escalation closure it is given and, when that closure signals, ends the process with ACL2's exit code (fnn-exit). The checker verifies the body ends in (handler-case (funcall install) (serious-condition ... fnn-exit)); a caller's closure must call a classifying_escape_function on the condition it escalates (checked at the escalation loop of fnn-mux-close-wake).

fnn-owner-run.why: A close hook that signals (fnn-pull-service-close re-signals a retained cleanup debt) clears modules-joined; the clean-close block needs it, so log-close-action stays the held value set before the hooks ran, and the not-joined arm returns fn-ort-log-close-exit with +fnn-exit-uncertain+, i.e. exit 3 (theorem fn-ort-log-close-held-is-uncertain). verify_close_hook_fences checks each link against owner.lisp and the book text.

nonblocking_leaves.sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown: shutdown(2) on a socket does not wait: it marks the half-connection closed and wakes blocked peers; SO_LINGER governs close(2), not shutdown(2). It still signals socket-error, which the failure rules (R7) see through the leaf's signal class. Deputy C2 ruling 2026-10-07.

fnn-mux-close-wake.why: close(2) of a pipe end does not block (Deputy C2 ruling 2026-10-07). verify_pipe_close_sites checks that the descriptor closed here is a let-bound read of the two wake slots, that every store into those slots in the host is NIL or a result of (sb-posix:pipe) (fnn-mux-start), and that no constructor call passes a slot keyword, so the slots hold only pipe ends.

binding_only_specials.*fnn-owner-deferred*: host/native/owner.lisp: the commit quantum's deferred list. It is bound only by let (fnn-owner-commit-start-locked, the next-batch seal in fnn-owner-commit-complete) to a fresh list; the checker verifies that no host form assigns the symbol, that its defvar value is NIL, and that every rebinding is a lexical variable or a list. Outside a quantum it is the constant NIL, so fnn-owner-log, fnn-owner-line-after-barrier and fnn-owner-feed-flush-after-barrier take their direct branch there (the open's key-statement recovery, an offline command).

enclave.comment: PROPOSED to the coordinator: the cold-read ownership protocol (books/page-read-direct.lisp) and the snapshot page lease -- the code already migrated onto issued rows/leases. Strict: no violation or unresolved site, no baseline rows.
enclave.files_why: lane ACTORS (rebuild step 0, the admin pilot): every owner section of host/native/admin.lisp is a declared def-section (fnn-quantum-control) and no function in it classifies a condition; strict by file, so a later hand wrapper or an undeclared quantum there fails --check with no baseline escape

realization_comment: SEED rows from build/coordinator/lanedumps/host-model.md REALIZATION; the authoritative copy becomes the host-model book's *fn-hmc-realization* defconst (agreed 2026-10-03). :retire, :window-acquire and :window-release and the P labels' sites are the deputy's to fill.
